data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves emerge singly at successive nodes along the stem, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped near the apex of the stem, giving a clustered appearance)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit consists of multiple leaflets attached to a rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaflet axis terminates in a single leaflet)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 16-20 (estimated from the longest, most complete leaflets visible)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are paired along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins are smooth without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate to oblong (leaflets are wider towards the tip and generally rectangular-oblong)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse to rounded (leaf tips are blunt and rounded)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf bases are rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (veins branch off a central midrib)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, pinnate, numerous, and arranged in a parallel fashion relative to each other
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (leaf surfaces appear matte, not glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible on the leaflets and rachis)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaflets)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not yet woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (hairs are visible on the main stem)
    19. Stem color: green to brown (stem color varies from green near the top to brownish lower down)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem appears relatively smooth, though hairy)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): present (small, pointed stipules are visible at the base of the petiole where it joins the stem)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct swelling at the base of the petiole is visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling is growing against a rough, dark brown tree trunk. Some leaflets show small holes. The overall leaf structure is bipinnate, though the images primarily show the pinnate leaflets. The lighting is natural and diffuse.
